subject.title: Workspace symlinks to ~/.openclaw subdirectories are rejected by boundary path check

question: Should fixed workspace bootstrap files be allowed to follow symlink targets outside the workspace, and if so which external roots are allowed or denied?
rationale: This changes which local filesystem locations can feed automatic startup prompt context, so the safe boundary is a maintainer security/product decision rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Define a narrow allow/deny policy
options.body: Allow only fixed bootstrap symlink targets that pass an explicit approved-root policy, while rejecting private OpenClaw state roots and direct arbitrary .openclaw paths.

options.title: Keep workspace-root-only
options.body: Leave current fs-safe behavior in place and document copy or sync workflows if external prompt authority is too risky.

options.title: Resolve through the overlapping PR
options.body: Use the open symlink PR only after it is rebased and explicitly covers this .openclaw sibling policy with tests.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow allow/deny policy
recommendation.body: Allow only fixed bootstrap symlink targets that pass an explicit approved-root policy, while rejecting private OpenClaw state roots and direct arbitrary .openclaw paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This person already kept the issue open with the concrete next-fix shape and owns the overlapping maintainer-labeled PR.
